project.name: pypi-ahmad
project.description: GitHub profile repository for Ahmad Mujtaba, an applied AI and GenAI engineer, showcasing documented work and automated profile assets.

nodes.name: github-stats.yml
nodes.summary: Scheduled GitHub Actions workflow that generates public-only GitHub language statistics and publishes the SVG assets to the generated branch.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses YAML workflow syntax with scheduled and manual triggers, shell validation, and branch publishing steps.

nodes.name: repo-cards.yml
nodes.summary: Scheduled GitHub Actions workflow that runs the repository card generator and publishes its rendered cards to the cards branch.
nodes.languageNotes: Runs a Python script on a daily schedule or manual dispatch, then publishes only changed card assets.

nodes.name: snake.yml
nodes.summary: Scheduled GitHub Actions workflow that generates contribution-snake SVGs and a 3D profile graph, publishing them to output and main branches.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses third-party GitHub Actions to generate visual assets on a daily schedule or manual dispatch.

nodes.name: _wrap
nodes.summary: Wraps card descriptions to bounded line and character limits, adding an ellipsis when text is truncated.

nodes.name: _esc
nodes.summary: Escapes text for safe insertion into SVG attributes and content.

nodes.name: _render_svg
nodes.summary: Renders a themed, escaped SVG card from repository metadata, including title, description, language, and activity details.

nodes.summary: Parses CLI options, loads selected repositories, fetches metadata, and writes light and dark SVG cards.

tour.title: Profile Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand this repository's purpose: an applied-AI engineering profile backed by selected work, outcomes, and generated visual assets. It also shows where repository cards and activity graphics appear in the public profile, providing context for the automation explored next.

tour.title: Repository Card Generator
tour.description: The card generator is the primary executable component: it fetches GitHub repository metadata and produces themed SVG cards for the README. Its broad fan-out makes it the best code-level map of how repository-list input becomes published profile output.

tour.title: Input And API
tour.description: The generator begins by parsing the curated repository list, then builds GitHub REST endpoints and retrieves metadata with retry handling. This separates user-maintained selection from remote API access before any presentation work begins.
tour.languageLesson: Python dataclasses model immutable values such as repository metadata, while urllib keeps the GitHub request path within the standard library.

tour.title: Card Rendering
tour.description: Repository responses become RepoInfo values and theme settings before SVG rendering formats each card. Text wrapping and HTML escaping protect the generated markup from malformed descriptions while keeping fixed visual bounds.

tour.title: Automation Workflows
tour.description: GitHub Actions schedules the repository-card generator and separately refreshes statistics and contribution visualizations. These workflows turn the profile from a static README into a maintained set of public artifacts without embedding runtime application services.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows use triggers to start jobs and ordered steps to run scripts or third-party actions before publishing generated assets.

tour.title: Contribution Standards
tour.description: The contribution guide sets expectations for focused changes, local validation, security reporting, and respectful participation. Read it with the conduct policy and security policy to understand the repository's maintenance boundaries before proposing a change.

tour.title: History And Analysis
tour.description: The changelog records user-facing evolution, while Graphify's report documents an independent generated view of repository structure. Together they distinguish maintained project history from disposable analysis output and make later automation changes easier to audit.
